questions.q: Article vs report — which opener is article-register: 'The fest was held on 5 May' or 'Five hundred students, zero phones, one unforgettable evening — this year's fest rewrote the rules'?
questions.a: The second — articles may perform voice and scene; reports must front-load plain facts. A wrong answer shows genre-boundary confusion.

questions.q: What format elements does an article need that an essay does not?
questions.a: A catchy title and a byline ('By Name, Class'). Essays carry no byline. A wrong answer 'subject line' imports the letter format.

questions.q: Is 'Yo, phones are literally destroying our brains fr' acceptable in a school-magazine article?
questions.a: No — articles allow voice but hold semi-formal register; slang breaks the contract. A wrong answer shows the student over-corrected from formal to casual.

questions.q: A ______ article balances personality and structure: catchy title + byline → engaging intro (question/anecdote) → 2-3 body paragraphs developing the idea → conclusion with a takeaway or suggestion.

Fill in the blank: A school-magazine article balances ______ and structure: catchy title + byline → engaging intro (question/anecdote) → 2-3 body paragraphs developing the idea → conclusion with a takeaway or suggestion.

Fill in the blank: The genre sits between report and essay: a report forbids voice; an article invites it; an essay argues a thesis. 'Social media: friend or foe?' can carry opinion-flavored analysis — but slang and ranting break the semi-formal ______.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes an article with title+byline, an engaging (not announcing) opening, developed body paragraphs, and a takeaway conclusion — distinguishing article register from both report and essay.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The genre sits between report and essay: a report forbids voice; an article invites it; an essay argues a thesis. 'Social media: friend or foe?' can carry opinion-______ analysis — but slang and ranting break the semi-formal contract.
